name: United States

areaKm2.note: world_1960 United States polygons (contiguous states, Alaska, Hawaii) = ~9.25M km2 computed on the sphere (low). Land plus inland water ~9.37M km2 used as mid; total incl. coastal and Great Lakes waters ~9.63M (high).

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop 1989 = 247,342k (mid). OWID population CSV (HYDE/UN) 1989 = 250.68M (high). Census Bureau mid-1989 estimate ~246.8M (low, from memory). 50 states + DC.

urbanization.note: OWID urban share United States 1989 = 75.4% (national definition).

activePersonnel.note: COW NMC v7 milper 1989 = 2,240k (high). End-FY1989 DoD active strength ~2.13M (Army ~770k, Navy ~593k, USMC ~197k, USAF ~571k; from memory, low). The US Army article notes plans in Nov 1989 to cut Army end strength from 750,000 to 580,000. Coast Guard excluded.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess: Selected Reserve ~1.17M (Army National Guard ~457k, Army Reserve ~319k, Air Guard ~116k, Air Force Reserve ~83k, Naval Reserve ~150k, Marine Reserve ~44k) plus part of the Individual Ready Reserve (~450k), as in the IISS Military Balance 1989-90 (not fetched). Guard brigades needed 60-90 days for combat readiness in 1990, so not all is callable in 30 days.

supportPersonnel.note: Active personnel minus the P roles: Navy (~593k), Air Force (~571k), Marine aviation and support, Army armor, artillery, aviation, air defence, engineer, signal, logistics and staff (2.2M - ~290k infantry).

mobilizationRatio.note: WWII benchmark: about 16.1M Americans served 1941-45 out of ~132-140M (~0.12); 12.2M under arms at the 1945 peak (~0.09). High allows a larger 1989 population share in total war.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Infantry of the 18 active Army divisions (6 armored, 6 mechanized/infantry with ~4-5 mech infantry battalions each, ~800 riflemen per battalion) plus 3 active Marine divisions (~9 infantry battalions each). Reconstruction from division structure; Guard divisions are reserves.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: M2 Bradley IFV, TOW, Dragon, M16A2; era-best mechanized infantry kit

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: all-volunteer long-service force, NTC Fort Irwin rotations since 1982

count.note: Infantry of the 82nd Airborne, 101st Air Assault and the 7th, 10th and 25th light divisions (~10,700 men each), 75th Ranger Regiment and Special Forces groups; about 60% of light division strength is infantry.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: UH-60 airmobility, night vision, but light anti-armour only

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: elite airborne and Ranger units; Panama (Dec 1989) showed high proficiency

count.note: Educated guess: M109 (~2,500) and M110 (~1,000) SP howitzers, ~2,000 towed M101/M102/M114/M198 (Army and USMC), ~470 MLRS launchers; Guard units included. Reconstruction from memory of the IISS Military Balance 1989-90.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: MLRS, Copperhead, TACFIRE fire direction, counter-battery radars

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: professional artillery branch

count.note: M1 Abrams article: 3,273 M1/IPM1 built 1979-85 and 4,753 M1A1 for the Army 1985-93 (roughly 3,000 delivered by mid-1989), so ~6,300-7,000 Abrams; plus ~8,000 M60A1/A3 in Army active and Guard units and ~716 USMC M60A1. IISS Military Balance 1989-90 gives a total near 15,600 (not fetched). Includes Guard and stored tanks.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: M1A1 with 120 mm gun and DU armour among the best tanks of 1989; M60A3 a generation older

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: NTC force-on-force training, gunnery tables; Desert Storm 1991 confirmed

count.note: Educated guess: M2/M3 Bradley ~6,000 delivered by 1989, M113 family ~22,000, LVTP-7 ~1,300 (USMC), plus M88/M577 variants partly counted. Totals as remembered from the IISS Military Balance 1989-90.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Bradley with TOW and 25 mm; M113 dated

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: professional crews

count.note: Educated guess: F-15 (~900), F-16 (~1,600), F-4 (~800, mostly Guard/Reserve), Navy F-14 (~420) and Navy/USMC F/A-18 (~600). Active plus Guard and Reserve; reconstruction from memory of the IISS Military Balance 1989-90.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 1.0. Evidence: F-15C/F-14/F-16 with AIM-7/AIM-9M, AWACS support: best in era

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Red Flag, Top Gun, ~20 flight hours per month

count.note: Educated guess: B-52G/H (~260), B-1B (97), FB-111 (~60), F-111 (~300), A-10 (~600), A-6 (~330), A-7 (~400), AV-8B (~200), F-117 (~50, secret until Nov 1988). Reconstruction from memory of the IISS Military Balance 1989-90.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: stealth F-117, laser-guided bombs, cruise-missile carrying bombers

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Red Flag, SAC readiness

count.note: Educated guess: Army ~8,600 (UH-1 ~3,500, UH-60 ~1,000, AH-1 ~1,100, AH-64 ~550, OH-58, CH-47 ~450) plus Navy/USMC ~1,800 and USAF ~200. Reconstruction from memory of the IISS Military Balance 1989-90.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: AH-64 Apache with Hellfire the best attack helicopter of 1989

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Army aviation branch, night flying

count.note: Educated guess: RQ-2 Pioneer systems bought 1986-89 for the Navy and Marines (~9 systems of 5-8 air vehicles); Army Aquila cancelled 1987. Group 3 only.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: early tactical UAV, line-of-sight datalink

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: new capability

count.note: 600-ship Navy article, build-up table 1989 column (from NHHC force levels): 17 carriers (incl. training carrier Lexington), 4 Iowa battleships, 41 cruisers, 63 destroyers, 104 frigates, 13 LHA/LPH/LHD = 242.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 1.0. Evidence: Aegis cruisers, nuclear carriers, Tomahawk; era best

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: blue-water navy with continuous deployments

count.note: 600-ship Navy article 1989 column: 21 mine-warfare ships, 10 PHM hydrofoils and gunboats, 10 LSD, 15 LPD, 5 LKA, 20 LST + 4 LSV, 2 LCC = 87. High adds Coast Guard cutters under Navy control in war.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: mine warfare force small and old (Aggressive class), Avenger class entering

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional crews

count.note: 600-ship Navy article 1989 column: 94 attack submarines (42 Los Angeles, 37 Sturgeon, ...) and 38 SSBN (10 Ohio, 28 Lafayette/Franklin/Madison/Ethan Allen) = 132.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 1.0. Evidence: quietest SSNs of the era, Trident II entering service 1990

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: nuclear navy selection and training

count.note: Launchers: 1,000 ICBM silos (950 Minuteman II/III, 50 Peacekeeper; the Minuteman article gives 1,000 Minuteman deployed from the 1970s, 50 converted to Peacekeeper 1986-88) plus ~100 Lance launchers; Pershing II and GLCM launchers were being eliminated under the INF Treaty (completed May 1991) so only some remain mid-1989 (high). SLBM tubes are in submarines.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: MX/Peacekeeper with 10 MIRVs, accurate Minuteman III

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: SAC missile crews, high alert rates

count.note: Educated guess: Batteries: Patriot (~60 fire units in 1989), Improved Hawk (~70 Army, USMC and Guard batteries), Chaparral/Vulcan batteries in divisional ADA battalions (~150). Stinger teams excluded. Reconstruction from division structure.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Patriot PAC-1 the most modern Western SAM

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: professional ADA branch

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.75. Evidence: AirLand Battle doctrine (FM 100-5, 1982/86), Goldwater-Nichols joint command reform 1986; Grenada 1983 showed joint friction, Panama (Dec 1989) went well

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75. Evidence: all-volunteer professional force recovered from post-Vietnam hollow army; strong unit identity

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Reagan-era rebuilding, high recruit quality; no recent major war

weapons.note: Anchor: weapons 9 (1985: guided missiles, MBTs with FCS, jets). Evidence: M1A1, Bradley with TOW, Tomahawk, Patriot, laser-guided bombs; above the 1985 anchor

armor.note: Anchor: armor 9 (composite armour). Evidence: M1A1 Chobham-type composite with depleted-uranium inserts (heavy armor 1988)

ships.note: Anchor: ships 9 (nuclear subs, Aegis). Evidence: Ticonderoga Aegis cruisers, Arleigh Burke 1991, Los Angeles SSNs, nuclear carriers

fortification.note: Anchor: fortification 9 (hardened shelters). Evidence: hardened aircraft shelters in Europe, hardened ICBM silos and NORAD Cheyenne Mountain

logistics.note: Anchor: logistics 9 (containerised, airlift). Evidence: C-5/C-141 strategic airlift, fast sealift ships, prepositioning (MPS squadrons from 1984)

communications.note: Anchor: communications 9 (satellite comms, data links). Evidence: DSCS and FLTSATCOM satellites, Link 11/16, MSE mobile subscriber equipment

isr.note: Anchor: isr 9 (satellites). Evidence: KH-11 imaging satellites, E-3 AWACS, JSTARS prototype, U-2/TR-1, SR-71 retired 1990

air.note: Anchor: air 9 (1985). Evidence: F-15C, F-16C, F-14, F-117 stealth, B-1B, B-2 first flight July 1989

cyber.note: Anchor: cyber 9 = 1990 networks. Evidence: ARPANET/MILNET and DDN in service; Morris worm Nov 1988 prompted CERT; NSA computer security center; just below the 1990 anchor

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID CSV) United States 1989 = 36,756 (2011 int$).

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI military expenditure share of GDP (OWID CSV): 1988 = 6.07%, 1989 = 5.87%, 1990 = 5.61%. COW milex 1989 = $294.9bn current.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: industry (manufacturing, mining, construction, utilities) roughly 28-30% of US value added in the late 1980s.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of the labour force (share of food output not eaten by the farm population; no calorie self-sufficiency adjustment). World Bank WDI Database Archives (version 1999 Apr), SL.AGR.TOTL.ZS "Labor force in agriculture (% of total)" (ILO-based) USA 1989 = 2.9%. Range 2-4%. The US was a large net food exporter. Share 2.9% (range 1.0-4.0%) -> 0.971 (0.96-0.99).

annualCohort.note: Educated guess: males reaching 18 in 1989 = males born 1971 (~3.56M US births, about 51% male) less mortality and plus immigration.

artillery.note: Soviet Military Power 1989 production table: US towed plus SP field artillery and MRLs 1986-88 roughly 150-350 per year; high is a wartime surge.

armor.note: Soviet Military Power 1989, table Production of Ground Forces Materiel: US tanks 1986-88 roughly 730-950 per year (OCR of the table). High = wartime surge with Lima and Detroit plants on extra shifts (educated).

ifv_apc.note: Soviet Military Power 1989 production table: US other armoured fighting vehicles 1986-88 ~800-1,300 per year; high is a wartime surge.

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess: F-16, F-15, F/A-18 and F-14 deliveries ~450-550 per year in 1987-89; high is a wartime surge.

aircraft_strike.note: Educated guess: A-6E, AV-8B, F-15E, B-1B (completed 1988) deliveries; high is a wartime surge.

helicopters.note: Educated guess: UH-60, AH-64, SH-60, CH-53E deliveries ~500-600 per year.

ships_major.note: Educated guess: Ticonderoga, Burke, Oliver Hazard Perry and Wasp-class completions late 1980s ~6-10 per year.

submarines.note: Educated guess: Los Angeles (~4 per year) and Ohio (~1 per year) completions.

missiles.note: Educated guess: ICBM and Lance launchers; production of launchers is small in peacetime.

air_defense.note: Educated guess: Patriot fire units and Hawk batteries fielded per year.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: about 3.6M km of paved roads of ~6.2M km public roads in the late 1980s; Interstate system ~70,000 km.

railKm.note: Educated guess: Class I railroad route ~236,000 km in 1989 after 1980s abandonments; high includes regional lines.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: major container and naval ports on three coasts and the Great Lakes (New York-New Jersey, Hampton Roads, Baltimore, Charleston, Savannah, Houston, New Orleans, Long Beach-Los Angeles, Oakland, Seattle-Tacoma, ...).

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: US-flag merchant fleet ~21M dwt in 1989 (privately owned plus Ready Reserve Force); high adds effective US-controlled flags of convenience.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: global power projection: strategic airlift, sealift and prepositioning; Desert Shield 1990 moved corps-size forces ~12,000 km.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: horses and mules in the US ~5M in the late 1980s; militarily irrelevant.

nuclearWarheads.note: FAS estimate (Kristensen and Korda, via OWID nuclear-warhead-stockpiles CSV) United States 1989 = 22,217 stockpiled warheads; range for Bulletin Nuclear Notebook variants.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: familiar terrain, local supply and strong population support; two-ocean isolation makes invasion near-impossible but the rubric has no ocean row.

notes: Snapshot date mid-1989 (IISS Military Balance 1989-90 basis, data as of 1 July 1989), before the fall of the Berlin Wall and the Panama intervention. Population convention: 50 states + DC; Puerto Rico and Guam excluded from population, Guam listed as a base. About 320,000 personnel were stationed in Europe (~250,000 in West Germany) and ~45,000 in Korea, so part of forces is forward-deployed. Ship counts come from the NHHC-based 600-ship Navy table; aircraft, armour, artillery and helicopter totals are reconstructions from memory of the IISS Military Balance 1989-90 (not fetchable) and are grade C/D; Guard and Reserve equipment is included in forces, Guard and Reserve personnel in trainedReserves. P-role splits are reconstructions from division structure. ships_major includes LHA/LPH amphibious assault ships; other amphibious ships are ships_minor. Cyber is rated by tech-anchor interpolation below the 1990 anchor.
